scores.claim_text: Kratos is positioned on the U.S. Air Force Skyborg program (Vanguard transitioning to Programs of Record in Dec 2022) and on the broader Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) family of next-generation autonomous wingman drones, framed as a primary forward-revenue platform.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='Collaborative Combat Aircraft', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') returned pe_number 0207147F with signal UNFUNDED_THIS_YEAR (FY24 funded_M=0.0) — at the cutoff the FY24 J-Book line for CCA shows zero, consistent with CCA having only just been carved out as a distinct PE in PB 2025.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Skyborg', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND (corpus does not contain a Skyborg-named PE — Skyborg was an AFRL Vanguard line that transitioned into CCA/ACP umbrellas).

Materiality test (heuristic 2 line 3): Kratos frames CCA/Skyborg as a FUTURE pipeline ('the DoD has stated they intend to field a family of new next generation drone aircraft, including CCAs'), not as booked revenue with concentration percentages. Narrative-load-bearing future claim with UNFUNDED PE -> downgrade to MODERATE.
scores.interpretation: At the 2024-09-01 cutoff, the CCA PE (0207147F) shows zero FY24 funding in the J-Book corpus. The materiality test downgrades severity: Kratos is positioning for CCA, not yet booking material CCA revenue. Concern remains because Kratos hinges growth narrative on Skyborg-to-CCA transition; Increment-1 awards announced earlier in 2024 went to General Atomics + Anduril (publicly disclosed pre-cutoff), with Kratos not selected as an Increment-1 prime. The filing does not disclose Increment-1 exclusion. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.

scores.claim_text: Kratos holds a 5-year, $400M IDIQ ceiling for development, integration and prototype air vehicle delivery in support of the Air Force Skyborg program (awarded July 2020) plus a $37.7M Skyborg Delivery Order 2 for XQ-58A Valkyrie aircraft (Dec 2020).
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='Skyborg', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND -- Skyborg is not a standalone PE in the FY26 corpus; subsumed into CCA (0207147F) and Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (0207179F).

pentagon_jbook(contractor_name='Kratos', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND -- Kratos is not listed as a primary_contractor in the J-Book corpus for any of the 410 PEs (heuristic 7: partial coverage, not necessarily red flag).
Original July-2020 IDIQ is a ceiling ($400M / 5 yrs ending July 2025) -- the forward issue is delivery-order flow post program-of-record transition.
scores.interpretation: $400M is a ceiling, not booked. With Skyborg subsumed into CCA at the cutoff, and Kratos not on the public Increment-1 award list, future Skyborg delivery orders are at risk after the 2025 IDIQ expiry. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: narrative implies forward continuity but the program-of-record transition introduces material risk that delivery orders flow through CCA primes (GA, Anduril).

scores.claim_text: XQ-58A Valkyrie tactical drone is a forward-looking platform with multi-customer order book (USAF AFRL, USMC, USN) and Kratos is producing two lots of 12 Valkyrie drones each, framed as a major future production line.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='XQ-58 Valkyrie', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND (corpus does not have an XQ-58-named PE).

pentagon_jbook(program_name='Autonomous Collaborative Platforms', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = FUNDED_STEADY, PE 0207179F, FY24 funded_M=$110.945M -- this is the umbrella PE under which XQ-58 development continues post-Skyborg.
pentagon_jbook(pe_number='0207179F', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = FUNDED_STEADY -- same PE, confirms steady ~$111M at FY24.
The November 2023 PAACK-P (USMC) test flight is recent and the December 2022 NAVAIR $15.5M XQ-58 buy is a real recurring procurement signal (heuristic 6 cross-check).
scores.interpretation: The Autonomous Collaborative Platforms PE -- the umbrella line for autonomous wingman R&D into which Skyborg flowed -- is FUNDED_STEADY at $111M FY24. XQ-58 Valkyrie production is plausibly supported by this funding plus separate Navy/USMC procurement. PASS at the cutoff: forward platform funding is real, not zeroed.

scores.claim_text: Kratos identifies USAF BQM-167, USN BQM-177, and GBSD (Sentinel) as programs that 'could represent a large portion of our future revenues in the coming years,' warning the loss or cancellation of any would adversely affect results.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='Aerial Targets', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = FUNDED_STEADY, PE 0305116F, FY24 funded_M=$6.671M (this is the RDT&E PE for aerial targets including BQM-167 development; procurement dollars live in P-40 line items not in this RDT&E PE).
pentagon_jbook(pe_number='0305116F', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = FUNDED_STEADY -- confirms PE active.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Sentinel', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND -- Sentinel/GBSD ICBM PE not in corpus.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='GBSD', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND -- same.
scores.interpretation: RDT&E PE 0305116F (Aerial Targets) is FUNDED_STEADY, supporting BQM-167/177 R&D continuation. Sentinel/GBSD: NOT_FOUND in corpus -- the corpus covers AF RDT&E Vol I-IV but the Sentinel ICBM is a strategic missile procurement / Air Force Procurement line; heuristic 7 says NOT_FOUND != red flag. Kratos' Sentinel exposure is via microwave/electronic-subsystem subcontracting through Northrop Grumman, which is well-documented and the Sentinel program at the cutoff was experiencing a Nunn-McCurdy critical breach (publicly known pre-cutoff) but had not been cancelled -- DoD reaffirmed Sentinel in July 2024. PASS at the cutoff for the named portfolio; some sub-program concern but not a J-Book divergence signal.

scores.claim_text: Jan-2023 $49.5M FRP Lot 4 award from NAVAIR for 55 BQM-177A surface-launched aerial targets and continued follow-on production lots, framed as a recurring procurement program.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='BQM-177', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND -- the corpus does not include the Navy P-40 aerial-targets procurement line item where BQM-177 production sits.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Aerial Targets', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = FUNDED_STEADY (PE 0305116F, the AF RDT&E side; Navy procurement is a separate line).
Heuristic 8: BQM-177 is a Navy PROCUREMENT line (P-40), not an RDT&E PE. Corpus is AF RDT&E + select procurement; Navy production lots are in N/Other Procurement P-40 lines not covered.
Crosswalk evidence: contracts file shows PIID N0001923C0021 = $238.8M 'SUBSONIC AERIAL TARGET (SSAT) BQM-177A FULL RATE PRODUCTION' -- Kratos really has Navy production funding.

M_value.secondary: FUNDED_STEADY for AF Aerial Targets PE 0305116F

scores.interpretation: BQM-177 procurement sits in Navy P-40 lines outside the corpus scope. Cross-check from the ticker_pe_crosswalk shows Kratos has $238M+ of obligated SSAT contracts, confirming the past-revenue claim is real. No J-Book divergence signal -- PASS.

scores.claim_text: Forward exposure to hypersonic test-bed market via MACH-TB subcontract and Mayhem Hypersonic System (sub to Dynetics).
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='MACH-TB', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Mayhem', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='hypersonic test bed', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
Corpus has 41 hypersonic-mentioning programs but no specific MACH-TB or Mayhem PE -- heuristic 7 says NOT_FOUND is UNVERIFIABLE for items the corpus may not cover.
scores.interpretation: MACH-TB is a relatively new Navy STRATCOM hypersonic test bed program; Mayhem is AFRL/Dynetics. Both are real programs but not in the FY26 J-Book corpus (likely Navy procurement P-40 / AFRL specialized lines). Kratos' role is as subcontractor not prime. UNVERIFIABLE -- coverage gap, not a J-Book divergence.

scores.claim_text: Kratos received a $54M AFRL Turbine Engine Division (AFRL/RQT) task order to develop a low-cost, limited-life jet engine for attritable and expendable systems, framed as a new prime engine business line tied to LCAAT efforts.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='LCAAT', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Low Cost Attritable Aircraft', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
pentagon_jbook(program_name='Turbine Engine Technology', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') = NOT_FOUND.
AFRL/RQT propulsion R&D PE is typically 0602203F (Aerospace Propulsion) -- not seeded in this corpus.
scores.interpretation: AFRL Turbine Engine work is a Title-III RDT&E PE not covered by this corpus. Heuristic 7: NOT_FOUND = UNVERIFIABLE. The $54M task order is a discrete award; absent visible J-Book coverage we cannot assess forward funding trajectory.

scores.claim_text: Kratos OpenSpace virtualized satellite ground system positioned with US Space Force / Space Development Agency (SDA) / Space Command as a forward growth program, with major awards from Blue Halo (~$160M for SCAR) and from Intelsat.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='Space Domain Awareness', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') matched 'Space Domain Awareness/Planning/Tasking SW' PE 1208248SF = FUNDED_STEADY, FY24 funded_M=$130.185M (this is a relevant umbrella PE for the OpenSpace narrative).

pentagon_jbook(program_name='SDA Transport Layer', cutoff_date='2024-09-01') matched PE 1206410SF -- the corpus has the Tranche 3 Transport Layer with status_declared UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS but at cutoff 2024-09-01 the M-source signal collapses to NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE because the unfunded years are FY26-FY27 (post-cutoff). At the 2024-09-01 cutoff, SDA Tranche 3 was still in pre-award competition; the eventual de-funding was post-cutoff and is correctly hidden by the cutoff filter.

Kratos' OpenSpace forward thesis depends heavily on SDA Transport Layer awards (the C2/ground-segment side). Tranche 0/T1 awards went to Iridium, Viasat, General Atomics, KBR ground-segment; Kratos is positioned on T2/T3 ground-segment competitions. The SDA T3 risk is not yet visible at cutoff.
scores.interpretation: Mixed signal: the Space Domain Awareness PE that backstops Kratos' OpenSpace business is FUNDED_STEADY at the cutoff. However, SDA Transport Layer (1206410SF), a known Kratos OpenSpace ground-segment opportunity, is flagged in the corpus as eventually UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS -- but that risk is post-cutoff. At 2024-09-01 with only FY24 visible, the analyst can only flag SDA as a concentration risk worth monitoring. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: Kratos' forward growth narrative leans on SDA Transport Layer / Space Force ground segment, an area where future-year visibility was weak at the cutoff (SDA leadership turnover, Tranche 3 RFP delays publicly discussed in 2024).

scores.claim_text: Kratos generated 69% of total revenue in fiscal 2023 from US Government contracts (vs 69% FY22, 70% FY21).
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts cross-check (ticker_pe_crosswalk): Kratos has 426 DOD contracts totaling $3.919B obligated -- consistent with high USG concentration disclosed.
Disclosure is candid and material; the 69% figure is steady across three years, not pivoting.
scores.interpretation: Standard concentration disclosure; no divergence. PASS.
